title: How to evaluate an agent for fixing a GitHub issue
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: An issue, a fixture repository, setup instructions and acceptance tests.
deliverable: A reviewable patch or pull request, test output and an explanation of remaining limitations.
steps: Agree on allowed files and dependencies
approval_boundary: Require approval for merging, release, production credentials and changes outside the fixture.
acceptance_criteria: Tests pass; the reported issue is addressed; unrelated behavior is preserved; a reviewer can reproduce the result.
failure_modes: Passing tests with a weakened assertion, unrelated refactors, hidden manual edits and a PR that does not address the issue.

title: How to evaluate AI pull-request review
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: A fixture pull request with known defects, acceptable changes and repository conventions.
deliverable: A set of findings with file references, severity, rationale and proposed remedies.
steps: Run the review without revealing the answer key
approval_boundary: Keep review comments separate from automatic code changes and merges.
acceptance_criteria: Measure defect recall, actionable precision, false positives, latency and reviewer time.
failure_modes: Counting every comment as useful, treating style opinions as defects and measuring only the number of findings.

title: How to evaluate agents for web data extraction
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: An allowed set of URLs, a required output schema and examples of missing or conflicting values.
deliverable: Structured rows with source URLs, observation times and explicit missing values.
approval_boundary: Use permitted public pages or a fixture. Do not grant form submission or purchase rights for a read-only extraction task.
acceptance_criteria: Field accuracy, source coverage, duplicate rate, missing-value handling and cost per accepted row.
failure_modes: Guessing missing fields, mixing prices from different plans, losing provenance and treating a browser session as a completed extraction.

title: How to test agents that complete browser workflows
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: A sandbox form, test account, permitted values and a clear final state.
deliverable: Completed fixture records plus screenshots or event logs showing the resulting state.
steps: Verify the backend or confirmation state
approval_boundary: Require a separate approval before sending external messages, submitting production records or committing purchases.
acceptance_criteria: Correct final state, duplicate avoidance, recovery from validation errors and intervention count.
failure_modes: Trusting the agent narrative, accepting a clicked button as success and retrying a submission that may already have succeeded.

title: How to evaluate customer support agents
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: An approved policy set, fixture customer records and tickets with known resolution paths.
deliverable: Grounded answers, correctly executed permitted actions and escalations with context.
steps: Review policy adherence and customer outcomes.
approval_boundary: Separate answer permissions from refunds, account changes, cancellations and disclosure of private data.
acceptance_criteria: Resolution quality, policy compliance, escalation quality, action correctness and cost per accepted resolution.
failure_modes: Calling a conversation resolved when it only ended, applying a policy to the wrong customer and suppressing escalation.

title: How to evaluate agents for account research
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: A target-company list, research questions, allowed sources and freshness requirements.
deliverable: A sourced account brief with uncertainty labels and suggested next steps.
approval_boundary: Keep external outreach disabled unless separately authorized. Avoid deriving sensitive personal attributes.
acceptance_criteria: Factual accuracy, source quality, freshness, entity resolution and time saved in review.
failure_modes: Confusing similarly named companies, treating a job posting as proof of deployed technology and inventing buying intent.

title: How to evaluate email infrastructure for agents
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: A sandbox inbox, fixture messages, intended thread behavior and a sending policy.
deliverable: Correctly received and classified messages, draft replies and a traceable test send when allowed.
approval_boundary: Separate read, draft and send authority. Define recipient checks, rate limits and escalation for sensitive content.
acceptance_criteria: Thread fidelity, delivery evidence, duplicate handling, classification quality and total workflow cost.
failure_modes: Confusing an API success response with inbox delivery, replying to the wrong thread and granting unrestricted sending to a research-only agent.

title: How to evaluate agents for invoice reconciliation
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: Synthetic invoices, purchase orders, payment records and a reconciliation policy.
deliverable: Matched records, explicit exceptions and an evidence trail for each proposed adjustment.
approval_boundary: Keep ledger posting and money movement outside the initial fixture test.
acceptance_criteria: Match accuracy, exception recall, duplicate detection and traceability to source documents.
failure_modes: Silently changing amounts, matching similar vendor names without identifiers and treating a recommendation as an approved accounting entry.

title: How to evaluate an MCP server before connecting it
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: The exact package or endpoint, version, client, documented authentication and intended tools.
deliverable: A versioned connection record, tool inventory and results from bounded fixture calls.
steps: Add write fixtures only within explicit limits.
approval_boundary: Never inherit permissions from a directory description. Review filesystem, network, account and secret access for the actual deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Connection success, tool-schema accuracy, authorization behavior, error handling and reproducible fixture results.
failure_modes: Confusing a registry URL with a repository, executing unreviewed install commands and calling a documentation MCP an execution service.

title: How to evaluate an agent skill
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: The exact skill directory and revision, instructions, resources and a representative task fixture.
deliverable: A dependency inventory, execution trace and accepted artifact.
steps: Verify the artifact against the fixture.
approval_boundary: Treat scripts and instructions as untrusted input until reviewed. Grant only the access required by the test.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact quality, reproducibility, dependency clarity, permission use and failure handling.
failure_modes: Assuming the skill name describes everything it can execute and treating a parent repository listing as an inspected skill implementation.

title: How to evaluate a paid API for agents
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: A documented endpoint, permitted budget, supported payment method and a known expected response.
deliverable: Payment and delivery evidence linked to a specific request and accepted response.
steps: Verify the delivered resource and receipt.
approval_boundary: Use a bounded wallet or payment mandate. This guide is a specification; this content package executes no payments.
acceptance_criteria: Total cost, authorization enforcement, delivery correctness, replay behavior and handling of a paid request that fails.
failure_modes: Counting a receipt as proof of useful delivery, confusing testnet with mainnet and ignoring fees or retry charges.

title: How to evaluate an agent task marketplace
intro: Use a bounded task with observable results. The candidates below are research starting points, not tested recommendations.
inputs: A bounded task, deliverable format, acceptance rubric, deadline and budget.
deliverable: Submitted work, a review decision and payment or dispute evidence where applicable.
steps: Record the result and settlement separately.
approval_boundary: Check who can accept work and release funds. Human fulfillment and autonomous-agent fulfillment are different service types.
acceptance_criteria: Accepted-task rate, rework, delivery time, evaluator independence and total cost.
failure_modes: Assuming a task board currently pays because older material mentioned payments, or treating self-attestation as independent acceptance.
